proposals.before: His wife, as her own daughter could not bear children, obtained the lady and cherished her more than a birth child; nurse and tutor instructed her, and her deportment was fully complete.
proposals.after: His wife, who had no daughter that lived (or could not raise a daughter of her own), obtained the lady and cherished her more than a birth child; nurse and tutor instructed her, and her deportment was fully complete.
proposals.reason: 息女不育 means the wife had no surviving/raised daughter of her own, not that a daughter was infertile.

proposals.before: His wife, who had no children of her own, took her in and loved her more than a daughter of her own blood; nurses and tutors trained her until her manners were flawless.
proposals.after: His wife, who had no daughter of her own that lived, took her in and loved her more than a birth child; nurses and tutors trained her until her manners were flawless.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic overgeneralizes 息女不育 to 'no children'; Chinese specifies daughter.

proposals.before: After he took the throne he posthumously invested her as Honored Consort and proclaimed mourning, which is why Shizong later issued an order for him to leave mourning.
proposals.after: After he took the throne he posthumously invested her as Honored Consort and proclaimed mourning; therefore there was an order for Shizong to leave mourning and resume office.
proposals.reason: 起復之命 applies to 世宗 (Shizong), not an order Shizong issued for Taizu; the translation reverses the referent.

decisions.after: His wife, who had no daughter that lived, obtained the lady and cherished her more than a birth child; nurse and tutor instructed her, and her deportment was fully complete.
decisions.reason: s0071 息女不育 means the wife had no surviving/raised daughter of her own, not that a daughter was infertile; the proposal’s parenthetical hedge is awkward, so a single clean rendering is used.
s0071 specifies 息女, a daughter; ‘no children’ overgeneralizes, and ‘no daughter … that lived’ restores the Chinese scope while keeping natural idiomatic English.
故世宗有起復之命 means Shizong was the one ordered to leave mourning and resume office; the prior English wrongly makes Shizong the issuer of an order for Taizu.
